chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ra'ab, from Abu Baseer, who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who has a slave girl in common with another partner, so one of them emancipates his share. The slave girl says to the one who did not emancipate: 'I do not desire you; appraise me and leave me as I am, serving you.' What is your view if the one who did not emancipate the other half intends to have sexual relations with her? Is that for him? He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not befitting for him to do that, because there do not be two private parts for the woman. And it is not befitting for him to make her serve [exclusively], but he should make her serve [alternately]. So if she refuses, there is a day for herself and a day for him.'

key_terms.يَطَأَهَا: He has sexual relations with her

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling when one partner frees his share of a slave girl and the remaining partner wants to have relations with her?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the jurisprudence of *shirkat al-umma* (partnership in a slave woman), where one owner frees his share while the other retains his. It establishes that the remaining owner cannot compel sexual relations if the woman prefers to remain in his service, nor can he force her into exclusive service if she refuses; instead, fairness is achieved through alternating days of availability. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the woman's agency and the equitable division of rights (*haqq*) between co-owners, preventing oppression (*zulm*) in domestic arrangements.
